    get:
      description: Returns a paginated list of dashboards. Each result includes title, description, tags, and metadata, but not the full panel layout. Use `GET /api/dashboards/{id}` to retrieve the complete state.
      operationId: get-dashboards
      parameters:
        - description: The page of results to return.
          in: query
          name: page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 1
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: The number of results to return per page.
          in: query
          name: per_page
          required: false
          schema:
            default: 20
            maximum: 1000
            minimum: 1
            type: number
        - description: Filters results by `title` and `description` using Elasticsearch [`simple_query_string`](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/query-languages/query-dsl/query-dsl-simple-query-string-query) syntax. Multi-word terms require all words to match.
          in: query
          name: query
          required: false
          schema:
            type: string
        - description: A tag ID to include. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are included.
          in: query
          name: tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag ID to exclude. Accepts a single tag ID or multiple tag IDs. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag IDs are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tags
          required: false
          schema:
            default: []
            description: Tag IDs associated with this dashboard.
            items:
              maxLength: 250
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
        - description: A tag name to include. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are included. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are included.
          in: query
          name: tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
            x-state: Generally available; added in 9.6.0
        - description: A tag name to exclude. Accepts a single tag name or multiple tag names. When multiple are specified, library items matching any of the tag names are excluded. If the same name is shared by multiple tags, items matching any of those tags are excluded.
          in: query
          name: excluded_tag_names
          required: false
          schema:
            items:
              type: string
            maxItems: 100
            type: array
            x-state: Generally available; added in 9.6.0

                      - dashboards

content.text:
I created the dashboard and the alert rule. Both exist, and the rule's first run completed with status `ok`.

**1. What the data holds.** Each document in `kibana_sample_data_logs` is one web request, with `timestamp` as the time field. The useful fields are:
- **Request:** `url`, `request`, `extension`, `referer`, `agent`.
- **Response:** `response` (the HTTP status code, stored as text, so I used `response.keyword`) and `bytes` (response size).
- **Client:** `clientip`, `geo.src` / `geo.dest`, `geo.coordinates`, `machine.os`, `machine.ram`.
- **Other:** `memory`, `phpmemory`, `tags`, `hour_of_day`.

**2. Dashboard "EFF-052c874d Web logs overview"** (id `120694d1-c79e-452a-8168-81cdefd91125`) has 8 panels and shows the last 7 days by default:
- **Headline numbers:** total requests, unique visitors (distinct `clientip`), average response size, and the number of 5xx server errors.
- **Requests over time:** stacked bars split by response code.
- **Response code mix:** a pie chart.
- **Top 10 requested URLs:** a table with request count and total bytes.
- **Top 10 source countries:** a table.

**3. Rule "EFF-052c874d 5xx spike"** (id `7f36cdcd-f39c-4002-8063-dc00b640442f`) is an Elasticsearch query rule. It runs every minute, counts documents where `response.keyword` is between 500 and 599 in the last 5 minutes (by `timestamp`), and fires when the count is more than 10. It has no notification actions, so when it fires the alert only shows up in Kibana. Add a connector, such as email or Slack, if you want to be notified.

The 5xx filters in the rule and in the error-count panel compare the code as text. That works here because every code is three digits.

I haven't checked whether the sample data has documents in the last 7 days. If the panels look empty, widen the time range.
